recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Treat the current Quantity model as governed by FHIR-51566 or any future comparator-related issue, not as an unapplied FHIR-22748 problem.
issue_request: FHIR-22748 asked for support for units on Observation.referenceRange because reference ranges may use units different from the Observation value. The Applied final resolution was Not Persuasive with Modification: revert the previous referenceRange datatype change and use SimpleQuantity because SimpleQuantity already includes units.
initial_application: Commit e9552da68ef21fe3c1c6e6ccb06a0771f5b80cd5 initially changed Observation.referenceRange.low/high from the SimpleQuantity profile to unprofiled Quantity for FHIR-22748. After the issue was reopened, commit c326984f5ac6ee9b4363c791e2ab01310b447ccd reverted low/high back to SimpleQuantity, matching the final FHIR-22748 disposition.
additional_context: Observation is active in source/fhir.ini. A later Applied OO issue, FHIR-51566, explicitly changed the same Observation.referenceRange.low/high elements from SimpleQuantity to Quantity for R6 so Quantity.comparator can represent exclusive bounds, with constraints limiting low/high comparator values and text preserving the inclusive default when comparator is absent. Current source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml reflects that later decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reverting current source to SimpleQuantity for FHIR-22748 would undo the later Applied FHIR-51566 decision, while the current Quantity datatype still supports value, unit, system, and code and therefore does not undermine the original unit-support concern.

related_jiras.note: Applied later OO decision for the same Observation.referenceRange.low/high elements; it intentionally changes them from SimpleQuantity to Quantity for comparator support.
